# Fathom

> AI can generate the work. Fathom helps you understand the work.

Fathom is an open-source, local-first CLI for project Work State. It reads observable repository evidence and reports what is in progress, what is complete, what changed, and what may be silently broken.

## Canonical links

- Repository: https://github.com/johnfaleke/Fathom
- Issues: https://github.com/johnfaleke/Fathom/issues
- Landing page: https://github.com/johnfaleke/Fathom/tree/main/site
- License: MIT

## Principles

- Local-first: no account or backend is required.
- Deterministic first: checks report evidence before any interpretation.
- Evidence-backed: findings include a category, severity, message, and evidence.
- Machine-readable: status, diff, and check support JSON output.
- Privacy-aware: no telemetry by default; secrets and .env values should never be sent to an AI provider.
- Open by design: Work State and the Check interface are public extension surfaces.

## Install and run

Install the published package globally:

```bash
npm install --global @johnfaleke/fathom
```

Then run it from any project workspace. The Fathom repository does not need to
be present there:

```bash
cd /path/to/project
fathom init
fathom set --current "Ship OAuth" --complete "Login API" --incomplete "Webhook retry"
fathom check
fathom status
fathom diff
```

For repository development, install dependencies and build from the Fathom repository:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
```

To analyze another project without a global install, run the built CLI while that project is the current working directory:

```bash
node /path/to/Fathom/dist/cli.js init
node /path/to/Fathom/dist/cli.js set --current "Ship OAuth" --complete "Login API" --incomplete "Webhook retry"
node /path/to/Fathom/dist/cli.js check
node /path/to/Fathom/dist/cli.js status
node /path/to/Fathom/dist/cli.js diff
```

For local development, `npm link` from the Fathom directory exposes the `fathom` command globally:

```bash
npm link
cd /path/to/project
fathom init
fathom check
fathom status
```

## Commands

- `fathom init`: creates `.fathom/` state, config, events, and `.env.example`.
- `fathom set`: records current work and comma-separated completed or incomplete work items.
- `fathom status`: reports current Work State, findings, and changed files.
- `fathom diff`: summarizes Git changes by project area. Requires a Git repository.
- `fathom check`: runs deterministic checks and exits with code 2 when warning findings exist.
- `fathom check --ai`: runs deterministic checks, then explicitly adds interpretation using the active profile.
- `fathom config show`: prints project configuration.
- `fathom config set ai.profile <name>`: selects a named AI profile without storing its API key.
- `fathom interpret --provider openai --consent`: explicitly sends filtered context to the configured provider for optional interpretation; requires `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

Add `--json` to `status`, `diff`, or `check` for automation.

## Local files

`.fathom/config.json` contains the version and explicit ignored directories. `.fathom/state.json` stores the current Work State. `.fathom/events.jsonl` stores append-only command observations. `.env.example` is the canonical environment reference used by the environment-variable check.

## Built-in checks

- `config.env-var-missing`: finds `process.env.X` usage without an entry in `.env.example`.
- `deps.undeclared-import`: finds imported packages missing from `package.json`.

## Work State shape

A Work State has `version`, `updatedAt`, `root`, `currentWork`, `completed`, `incomplete`, `findings`, `changes`, and `attention`. Findings use stable IDs, categories, one of `info`, `warning`, or `potential` severity, a message, and an evidence array.

## Extension interface

A check implements:

```ts
interface Check {
  id: string;
  run(ctx: ProjectContext): Promise<Finding[]>;
}
```

The public package exports `Check`, `Finding`, `Evidence`, `ProjectContext`, `WorkState`, `runChecks`, `createProjectContext`, and `builtinChecks`.

## Optional AI provider interface

AI interpretation is intentionally separate from deterministic evidence:

```ts
interface AIProvider {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  type: "openai" | "anthropic" | "google" | "custom";
  interpret(input: AIInterpretationRequest): Promise<AIInterpretationResult>;
}
```

Providers must be opt-in, clearly label interpretation, preserve underlying evidence, require consent for remote context, and never receive secrets or `.env` values.

The v0.2 CLI uses the OpenAI-compatible adapter through the simpler check flow:

```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key fathom check --ai --json
```

Optional `.fathom/config.json` policy:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "ignore": ["node_modules", "dist", ".git", ".fathom"],
  "ai": {
    "profile": "work",
    "profiles": {
      "work": {
        "provider": "openai",
        "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
        "apiKeyEnv": "OPENAI_API_KEY"
      }
    },
    "includePaths": ["README.md", "src/index.ts"],
    "maxFileBytes": 50000
  }
}
```

## Contribution path

1. Fork the repository.
2. Add or improve a deterministic check.
3. Include evidence in each finding.
4. Add a focused test.
5. Run `npm run build` and `npm test`.
6. Open a pull request explaining the observable behavior.

## Product status

Fathom v0.1 is the deterministic core. MCP, editor integrations, broader check packs, and production AI providers are later roadmap work.
